1. Validate the current bill: confirm meter reads imply 1,004 kWh (62,468 − 61,464), line items sum to $185.78 ($18.71 + $33.27 + $133.80), and the change versus last month is +$10.05 ($185.78 − $175.73); treat any arithmetic mismatch as a suspected billing error.

2. Map each billing period to its AEP Ohio tariff: last month (2026-03-04 to 2026-04-04) falls entirely under the pre-2026-04-10 tariff (fixed $18.38; variable $0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225/kWh for the first 2,000 kWh). The current period (2026-04-04 to 2026-05-05) straddles the 2026-04-10 change, so prorate the fixed charge ($18.38 vs $18.788) and blend the variable rate ($0.1607225 vs $0.0347738 + $0.13299 = $0.1677638/kWh) across the boundary.

3. Set days_usd = 0 because both periods are 31 days.

4. Estimate weather_usd from NOAA degree days: compare last month (CDD 16.5 / HDD 408) to current (CDD 43.5 / HDD 255.5), derive a weather-to-kWh coefficient from the bill history, convert the weather-driven kWh difference to dollars at the effective rate, or set weather_usd = 0 if no defensible coefficient can be estimated.

5. Compute price_usd from the tariff changes (higher fixed charge and higher blended variable rate) applied to baseline usage; compute usage_usd from the 25 kWh increase (979 → 1,004) valued at the effective rate; use usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly +$10.05.

6. Check for a billing error by comparing the tariff-modeled current-period total to the actual $185.78; if the difference exceeds rounding, set billing_error_suspected = true and billing_error_usd to the discrepancy, otherwise false and null.

7. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
